annotations.text:
Every screen is styled now.

Ink and paper, two greys, one accent (#3a577c) on links, focus and ghost buttons. Status colours: green published/ready/visible, grey draft, ochre pending, brick unavailable.

Buttons: primary filled, secondary outlined, ghost for row and inline actions.

Table headers hold one line, rows clamp to two.

IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for slugs, keys and endpoints.

Nuxt routes behind this shell:
/login
/ → redirect to /products
/products
/products/:id
/suppliers
/suppliers/:id
/media
/taxonomy/categories
/taxonomy/spec-attributes
/settings

Every page declares access: 'admin-only' except /login (guest).

Products and suppliers each get their own page — both carry more than a row's worth of editing. Categories and spec attributes stay inline under their list: a name, a slug, a unit, a parent, nothing that needs a page of its own.

Open question: the admin API has no media listing, only DELETE /admin/media/:id. Either add GET /admin/media, or drop the Media nav item and reach images only through the pickers in a product or supplier.

The supplier page's Contact section has nothing behind it. The suppliers table is name, slug, description, logo, visible — no contact person, phone, email, or location. Decide whether those columns get added or the section comes out.
Admin login is its own cookie and its own audience. A workshop session on the same browser is never accepted here.

The five sections here are five endpoints. Options, variants, specs and media are PUT — each save replaces the whole set, so they cannot share one Save button with Details (PATCH) without inventing a batch endpoint.

New product takes only what POST /admin/products accepts: supplier, category, name, slug, description. It saves as a draft and lands on the product page, where the five PUT sections are filled in. Publish stays a separate action, never a status field on this form.
